clue.text: Here, you may see Turandot left as her prince finally fails

indicators.note: the last letter of the name is lost, so the final letter drops away

parts.note: Calaf is the prince who wins Princess Turandot in Puccini's opera

explanation.surface: An opera fan watches Turandot as the hero's luck runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally fails' removes the F at the end of CALAF, leaving CALA. Turandot premiered at La Scala, the Milan opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan's famous opera house staged the premiere of Puccini's opera, so it is a place to see it performed.

clue.text: Hideout left open to the atmosphere

parts.note: to air something is to leave it open to the atmosphere

explanation.surface: A hiding place has been abandoned and left exposed to the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's den, or a criminal's base, is a hiding place.

clue.text: Burn to stay a minute in discussion group

indicators.note: the shortened minute is placed in the middle of the word for burn

parts.note: to sear is to burn

explanation.surface: A scorched delegate lingers for a moment at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small class or group meeting for discussion, especially at a university.

clue.text: Top removed from more exposed tree

indicators.note: the first letter, the top of a down entry, is taken off the word

parts.note: balder means having less hair, so the scalp is more exposed

explanation.surface: A tree loses its crown and stands more bare than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top removed from' takes the first letter B off BALDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a common waterside tree of the birch family.

clue.text: Gossip with those people's a curse

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes and gossip about a person
them stands for those people; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: Gossiping with certain folk is held to be a bane.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is a formal ecclesiastical curse, and by extension something detested.

clue.text: Is trapped in house beginning to collapse due to earthquake

indicators.note: the two-letter word is shut inside the word for a house

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, a British housing type joined to its neighbour

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck in a house that starts to fall down in a quake.
explanation.walkthrough: SEMI is British shorthand for a semi-detached house, one of a pair sharing a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Seismic describes something caused by or relating to earthquakes.

clue.text: Aussie woman, woman I associated with US city

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: An Australian woman is linked with an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheila is Australian slang for a woman or girl.

clue.text: Route I attempt to go round in a long time

indicators.note: the word for attempt is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: a try is an attempt
taken as written
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A traveller vows to complete a circuit over a lengthy period.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerary is a planned route or list of places on a journey.

clue.text: Infallible man-catcher has second set free

parts.note: a mo is a moment or second
to untie is to release

explanation.surface: A never-failing thief-taker has a moment to release someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police are proverbially said always to get their man.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mountie, a Canadian mounted policeman, is famed for always catching the wanted man.

clue.text: Laundry output showing unblemished record?

definitions.meaning: a freshly washed piece of bedlinen comes out of a laundry
a record with no black marks, or in football a match without conceding a goal

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a newly washed bedsheet and a record free of any offence.

clue.text: I'm to assist in negotiations, starting now

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
to mediate is to help two sides negotiate

explanation.surface: Someone volunteers to help with talks beginning straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate action is action taking effect at once, starting now.

clue.text: Get used to one health-worker, not second

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: the abbreviation for second is dropped from the word

parts.note: a nurse is a health worker

explanation.surface: A single nurse becomes accustomed to the job, not taking seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not second' removes S, the abbreviation for second, from NURSE, leaving NURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure is to accustom someone to something unpleasant until they no longer feel it.

clue.text: Town presenting tall tenor and horn in pieces

indicators.note: the words are broken apart and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written as part of the letter pool
taken as written as part of the letter pool

explanation.surface: A town puts on a concert featuring a lanky tenor and a broken horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in pieces' signals the anagram of TALL TENOR HORN. Northallerton is a market town in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Northallerton is the county town of North Yorkshire in England.

clue.text: Keeps cash-register stationary

parts.note: a shop stocks, or keeps, goods
a till is a cash register

explanation.surface: A shop holds onto its cash register that doesn't move.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-still means completely motionless.

clue.text: Annoying sore is treated in due course

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for due course

parts.note: in time means in due course

indicators.note: the sore is worked on and changed, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An irritating wound will heal, given time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is treated' looks like it describes the sore, but it is the anagram signal; 'in due course' is idiomatically 'in time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome means tedious and irritating.

clue.text: Official figure still holding rest up

indicators.note: the first word keeps the other inside it

parts.note: static means still or motionless

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to sit is to rest

explanation.surface: A government number stays fixed while holding back the remainder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the rest word because this is a down entry; 'holding' sets it inside the word for still.
explanation.definitionFit: A statistic is a numerical fact, such as an official published figure.

clue.text: Newspaper backed the misrepresented chap

indicators.note: the newspaper word is read backwards

parts.note: a rag is a low-quality newspaper

indicators.note: the word is shown wrongly, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tabloid supported a man who had been misquoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns RAG into GAR; 'misrepresented' scrambles THE into ETH.
explanation.definitionFit: Gareth is a man's name, and a chap is a man.

clue.text: Confused everyone in the main

parts.note: all means everyone
the main is the sea, so in the main is at sea

explanation.surface: Everybody in the ocean is bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old literary term for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To be all at sea is an idiom for being completely bewildered.

clue.text: Leaders of clothing retailers facing a tax for neckwear

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax

explanation.surface: Fashion shop bosses confront a sales tax on ties.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is value added tax, the British equivalent of a sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat is a wide scarf-like band worn around the neck.

clue.text: Arthur is an excellent craftsman

parts.note: Art is a short form of the name Arthur

explanation.surface: Arthur is praised as a superb maker of things.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled worker in a craft, valued for good workmanship.

clue.text: Drama before end of game for fellow-sportsman

parts.note: a play is a drama
mate, checkmate, is the end of a game of chess

explanation.surface: A theatrical show precedes the end of the match for a teammate.
explanation.definitionFit: A playmate is a companion one plays games or sport with.

clue.text: Insect, female, having upturned feeler

parts.note: an ant is an insect

indicators.note: in a down clue, upturned means the name is read from the bottom up

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name, standing for any female

explanation.surface: A female bug has an antenna pointing upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is an insect's sensory feeler on its head.

clue.text: "Go to blazes," I say, being upset about fool

indicators.note: the turned letters are placed around the fool
in a down clue, upset means the letters are turned upside down

parts.note: e.g., for example, is shorthand for say
a nit is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone angrily tells another to go to hell after being called an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being upset' reverses the abbreviation for say, and 'about' wraps it round the fool. The curse 'Go to blazes' is read literally as burst into flames.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite is to catch fire, literally to go up in blazes.

clue.text: One wouldn't stand for being attacked

definitions.text: One wouldn't stand for being attacked

parts.words: One wouldn't stand for being attacked
parts.note: reads as someone who will not tolerate assault, but means something seated and easy to hit

explanation.definitionFit: A target that is sitting, not standing, is an easy object of attack.

clue.text: Drink up last of wine in feast

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: grog is rum and water, or any alcoholic drink

indicators.note: the final letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: At a banquet someone finishes off the rest of the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to eat greedily, to feast.

clue.text: Drop live advertisement

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's live commercial is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A bead is a small drop of liquid, as in a bead of sweat.

clue.text: Small map, part of a series?

definitions.meaning: a little map placed within a larger one
read as two words, something in a set belongs to a series

explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small map within a larger one, and split it means included in a set.

clue.text: Car in use possibly involving new requirement for motorists?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation
the words could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A vehicle being driven needs a fresh legal necessity for drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CAR IN USE, and 'involving' puts N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor insurance is legally compulsory for drivers.

clue.text: Oxford college lecturer's first in field perhaps

indicators.note: the opening letter of the lecturer is taken

parts.note: an acre is a measure of land, such as a field

explanation.surface: A don is the first to arrive in a meadow, possibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Linacre College is a graduate college of Oxford University.

clue.text: A poet's written about the Spanish monk

indicators.note: the poet's word is set around the Spanish article

parts.note: a bard is a poet; the 's is a link meaning has
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A poet composes verses about a Spanish monk.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Abelard was a medieval French philosopher who became a monk after his affair with Heloise.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Abelard took monastic vows at the abbey of Saint-Denis.
